guide.title: Heart Failure & Pulmonary Edema
guide.lead: A drowning patient sitting bolt upright, with crackles, frothy sputum and a high BP, needs CPAP, nitrates and the seat back up, not a fluid bolus. Low BP changes everything: that's cardiogenic shock.

sections.title: Left or right?
rows: Breathlessness, orthopnea, night waking, crackles, pink frothy sputum
Raised JVP, leg and sacral edema, big liver
Left heart failure; lung disease; PE

sections.title: Acute pulmonary edema
sections.question: Is the systolic BP 90 mmHg or more?
sections.yes: Awake, protecting the airway and not vomiting: CPAP 5–10 cmH₂O. If not: assist ventilation with a BVM. Nitrates and diuretic per protocol; transport.
sections.no: Cardiogenic shock: no nitrates, no CPAP. Assist ventilation if failing; vasopressors (ALS); PCI centre if STEMI.

groups.title: Look for
items: Very high BP; kidney failure; PE

sections.title: Heart failure or COPD?
items: Wheeze can be "cardiac asthma" (swollen airway walls)
Crackles, raised JVP, edema and orthopnea point to the heart
CPAP helps both; don't delay it for nebulizers

quiz.q: Most effective prehospital treatment for acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema with a good BP?
quiz.explanation: Plus upright position and nitrates per protocol.

quiz.q: Raised JVP in suspected heart failure suggests:
options: Right-sided failure and high venous pressure
quiz.explanation: Tension pneumothorax and tamponade also raise it, so look at the whole picture.

quiz.q: Why sit a pulmonary edema patient upright?
options: Less venous return and easier breathing
quiz.explanation: Lying flat makes the hypoxia worse.
Also unresponsiveness, vomiting and suspected pneumothorax.
Fluid and blood in the alveoli.

quiz.q: Peripheral edema and a big liver point to:
quiz.explanation: Blood backs up into the body.

options: Stopping medicines or salt and fluid excess
quiz.explanation: Also ischemia, AF, infection and very high BP.

quiz.q: Nitroglycerin helps pulmonary edema mainly by:

quiz.explanation: Ask how many pillows they sleep on.

quiz.q: Typical CPAP starting pressure for pulmonary edema:
quiz.explanation: Titrate per protocol and watch the BP.

flashcards.question: Left vs right heart failure
flashcards.answer: Left: backs up into the lungs (crackles, orthopnea, frothy sputum). Right: backs up into the body (raised JVP, edema, big liver).

flashcards.question: Signs of acute decompensated heart failure
flashcards.answer: Breathlessness, orthopnea, night waking, raised JVP, edema, crackles, pink frothy sputum, sitting upright; high BP early, low BP ominous.

flashcards.question: Best prehospital treatment for pulmonary edema
flashcards.answer: CPAP: splints the alveoli open, lowers preload and work of breathing (with an adequate BP).

flashcards.question: Why keep them upright?
flashcards.answer: Less venous return and congestion, and better diaphragm movement. Lying flat worsens hypoxia.

flashcards.question: Triggers for decompensation
flashcards.answer: Stopped medicines, salt or fluid excess, ischemia, arrhythmia (AF), infection, very high BP, kidney failure, PE.

flashcards.question: Nitroglycerin in pulmonary edema
flashcards.answer: Venodilator: lowers preload and congestion. Only if systolic BP is 90 mmHg or more (or your protocol's threshold).

flashcards.question: Furosemide
flashcards.answer: Loop diuretic: diuresis plus early venodilation; slower than CPAP and nitrates, so give per protocol.

flashcards.question: Pink frothy sputum
flashcards.answer: Severe pulmonary edema: fluid and red cells in the alveoli. A late, ominous sign.

critical.scenario: A 78-year-old with heart failure ran out of her water pills 5 days ago. Tripoding, 2-word sentences. BP 168/100, HR 112, RR 32, SpO₂ 84%. Crackles halfway up, leg edema, raised JVP.
critical.question: Cause and priority?

options.t: Decompensated heart failure from missed medicines: sit up, CPAP, nitrates per protocol

options.f: Crackles, JVP and edema point to the heart.

critical.explanation: CPAP improves oxygenation and reduces preload and work of breathing; her BP allows nitrates.
critical.kpi: Recognizes ADHF from history and exam, initiates CPAP as priority intervention

critical.scenario: A 72-year-old with heart failure and COPD can't lie flat. Wheezes everywhere and fine crackles at the bases; mild JVP, ankle edema. BP 148/88, SpO₂ 89%.
critical.question: How do you read this?

options.t: Likely heart failure with "cardiac asthma": CPAP, adding a bronchodilator if wheeze persists
COPD only: nebulizers and never CPAP
options.f: CPAP is used in COPD exacerbations too.
Not with crackles and raised JVP.

options.t: Wait for wheeze to settle before CPAP

critical.explanation: Crackles, raised JVP, edema and orthopnea point to fluid overload even when wheeze is loud.
critical.kpi: Differentiates ADHF from COPD exacerbation and applies CPAP appropriately

critical.scenario: On CPAP for pulmonary edema, a 68-year-old first improved. Now she's lethargic: BP 72/40, HR 56, shallow breathing, SpO₂ 89%, EtCO₂ falling.
critical.question: What now?

options.t: Cardiogenic shock and failing breathing: remove CPAP, ventilate with a BVM and oxygen, prepare for arrest

options.f: More pressure lowers venous return further.
Falling consciousness and EtCO₂ mean falling cardiac output.

critical.explanation: Falling EtCO₂ with hypotension means less blood reaching the lungs. Have the pads on and call for ALS (vasopressors).
critical.kpi: Recognizes transition from ADHF to cardiogenic shock and initiates appropriate rescue ventilation
